newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CANSECO SMASH IN NINTH GIVES A'S 2-1 WIN OVER INDIANS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CANSECO SMASH IN NINTH GIVES A'S 2-1 WIN OVER INDIANS.

text.p: Jose Canseco smashed a 458-foot (140-metre) home run in the top of the ninth inning off Mike Jackson Friday to give the Oakland Atletics a 2-1 victory over the Cleveland Indians.
"I got a fastball middle away," Canseco said. "He may have tried to go four or five inches outside to try to get that called strike three, but he left it on the outer third of the plate."
Canseco's blast, his 21st of the season, was the first homer allowed by Jackson since September 8, when he was with Seattle -- a span of 59 1/3 innings and 53 appearances.
Canseco had been 0-for-17 lifetime against Jackson (2-2).
"I have faced him in the past and he's thrown me a lot of sliders," Canseco said. "I had that in the back of my mind so I just told myself to hit a lot deeper in the zone."

"With the stuff I have I think I match up against him," Jackson said. "He's a good hitter and it was just a matter of time until he got a hit off of me. It was the right time for him and the wrong time for me."
Canseco's home run was the 349th of his career, tying him for 49th on the all-time list with George Foster.
Aaron Small (7-4) pitched the eighth to get the win and Billy Taylor worked a perfect ninth to pick up his 19th save.
The Indians are now 2-6 on a homestand in which opponents have out-homered them 9-1,and Cleveland is batting only .252 as a team, scoring just 22 runs.

In New York, Ken Griffey Jr ended his longest homerless drought of the season with a three-run blast to cap a six-run fourth inning and Jamie Moyer (11-3) allowed one run over a season-high 7 1/3 innings as the Seattle Mariners rolled over the Yankees 8-1.

Griffey's opposite-field homer, his 31st, chased New York starter David Wells (10-5) and ended a 14-game homerless drought, a span of 59 at-bats. It also moved him past Joe Morgan, Brooks Robinson and Gorman Thomas into sole possession of 95th place on the all-time home run list with 269.
Alex Rodriguez had three RBI and Dan Wilson added a solo homer for Seattle, which has won three straight games.
New York had its three-game winning streak stopped but remained 3 1/2 games behind first-place Baltimore in the American League East.
In Boston, the Angels swept the Red Sox in a doubleheader at Fenway Park for the first time in 34 years.

In the opener, Chuck Finley allowed a run over seven innings to win his career-high sixth straight game and Tim Salmon homered and drove in three runs as Anaheim held on for a 5-4 victory over the Red Sox.

Finley (9-6) scattered seven hits and three walks with nine strikeouts. The left-hander has won his last six outings -- allowing 11 earned runs in 42 2/3 innings (2.32 ERA) -- after going 0-2 in his five previous starts.
In the second game, Tim Salmon hit a sacrifice fly and Garret Anderson added a two-run homer in the ninth in an 8-5 victory.
The Angels are 12-3 since the All-Star Break and have won 14 of their last 17 games.
In Chicago, pinch-hitter Mike Simms' two-run homer capped a three-run eighth and gave the Texas Rangers an 8-5 win over the White Sox, snapping a four-game losing streak.
The Rangers won for just the third time in 12 games.
Danny Patterson (7-4) got the win and John Wetteland worked a perfect ninth for his 20th save in 26 chances.

Robin Ventura, playing his second game of the season, had two hits, including a solo homer for Chicago, which has lost three of its last four games but remained 3 1/2 behind first-place Cleveland in the American League Central.

In Detroit, Dave Nilsson hit the first of his two homers back-to-back with Jeromy Burnitz in a three-homer fourth inning as the Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tigers 6-1, snapping a four-game losing streak.
Gerald Williams also homered off Scott Sanders (3-7) in the fourth.
Milwaukee had not hit three homers in an inning since May 17, 1996 against the Twins, when Nilsson hit two and Fernando Vina had the other.
At Minnesota, Paul Molitor hit two solo homers and drove in three runs and Brad Radke went the distance to win his 10th straight start as the Twins beat the Baltimore Orioles 5-2.

Radke (14-5) became the third 14-game winner in the American League, joining Toronto's Roger Clemens and Seattle's Randy Johnson. He allowed a pair of solo homers and seven hits with a walk and six strikeouts for his second straight complete game and third of the season.

In Toronto, Robert Person (4-6) allowed one run over 6 1/3 innings and Alex Gonzalez snapped a tie with a solo homer in the fifth as the Blue Jays edged the Kansas City Royals 2-1 for their season-high fourth straight victory.
